summary: BLOCKING RELEASE PREREQUISITE, now FOUR surfaces, unchanged since it was first raised in Wave 33. Four server-side fan-outs now refuse to make any outbound request unless an operator has declared an internal origin, because deriving the destination from the inbound request was the SSRF defect. The guard has NO fallback and NO localhost default, so an environment with none of these variables set does not error — it silently returns empty results. AFFECTED SURFACES, all in discover's charter, ALL FOUR NOW SILENTLY DEGRADED UNTIL THE VARIABLE IS SET: (1) GET /api/discover — the whole aggregation fan-out (posts, events, music, suggestions, people, albums, tours) returns empty sections. (2) GET /api/hub — discover + news + jobs sections return zeroed metrics. (3) GET /api/news/feed and GET /api/feed/for-you — the external RSS candidates are gone. (4) ADDED IN WAVE 35: POST /api/opportunities/sync and GET /api/opportunities?refresh=true — the opportunities RSS ingest upserts ZERO records and logs '[Opportunities] No internal upstream origin is allowlisted'. THE EXACT VARIABLES THE GUARD READS, IN PRECEDENCE ORDER, ALL SERVER-SIDE FROM process.env: INTERNAL_API_ORIGIN, then NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, then VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL, then VERCEL_URL. A value may be a space- or comma-separated list. A source whose value contains any unusable entry contributes NOTHING AT ALL, so a typo yields an EMPTY allowlist rather than a widened one — the failure mode is fail-closed. DISCOVER_ALLOW_LOCAL_UPSTREAM is a development-only opt-in and MUST BE UNSET in every deployed environment: a loopback or private-literal origin is refused outright when NODE_ENV=production even with it set. This is a named blocking acceptance criterion on DISC-002 as well as a blocker on that task.

Made each affected route log a distinct, actionable warning naming the variable to set, so the failure is diagnosable from logs instead of being a silent empty response. Before this the news surface had no signal at all.
Recorded the prerequisite as a named blocking item on DISC-002 acceptance and in its blockers, not only in a handoff.
Confirmed the guard fails CLOSED and never widens: no allowlisted origin means zero outbound requests, and a partially-parseable env value means zero allowlisted origins, not a subset.

Wave 35: the fourth surface was ADDED to this list rather than to a new handoff. POST /api/opportunities/sync (app/api/opportunities/sync/route.ts) and GET /api/opportunities?refresh=true (app/api/opportunities/route.ts:34) now call ingestOpportunitiesFromRss, which returns { upserted: 0 } and logs a warning naming INTERNAL_API_ORIGIN when the allowlist is empty. Before Wave 35 that call used a caller-supplied origin and therefore did work without the variable — so setting the variable is now REQUIRED for the opportunities ingest to function at all, where before it was only required for the other three.

next_steps: RELEASE/INFRA — ACTION 1, blocking: set INTERNAL_API_ORIGIN explicitly in EVERY deployed environment (production, staging, and every preview) to the app's own absolute https origin, for example https://app.tourify.app with NO path, query or fragment. Prefer it over relying on the Vercel-provided variables: VERCEL_URL is a per-deployment value and the preview origin changes on every deploy, so relying on it makes preview behaviour non-deterministic. The guard rejects a configured origin that carries a path, query, or fragment, so the value must be a bare scheme://host[:port].

RELEASE/INFRA — ACTION 2, blocking: leave DISCOVER_ALLOW_LOCAL_UPSTREAM UNSET in every deployed environment, including preview. It exists only for local development against http://127.0.0.1:3000 and is ignored when NODE_ENV=production. Do not add a development default for it in a shared env file.

RELEASE/INFRA — ACTION 3: grep the deploy configuration for all five names — INTERNAL_API_ORIGIN, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL, VERCEL_URL, DISCOVER_ALLOW_LOCAL_UPSTREAM — before promoting, and record in the release notes which environment each was set in, so a later wave does not have to re-derive it. This is the step that has been missed three waves running.

RELEASE/QA — SMOKE, all four surfaces, after the variable is set. Confirm NON-EMPTY, not merely 200: (a) GET /api/discover returns sections.for_you with items and stats.trending_count above zero; (b) GET /api/hub returns metrics.headlines above zero; (c) GET /api/news/feed returns at least one item whose originType is 'external'; (d) POST /api/opportunities/sync returns { upserted: 0 } WITH NO `[Opportunities] No internal upstream origin is allowlisted` warning, and a subsequent GET /api/opportunities returns rows. DIAGNOSING A FAILURE: an empty result WITH the warning means the allowlist is still empty (wrong value, wrong name, or a value carrying a path). An empty result WITHOUT the warning means the origin resolved but the upstream refused — check the `[News feed] Upstream "newsRssFeed" denied: <reason>` and `[Opportunities] Upstream "opportunitiesRssNews" denied: <reason>` log lines, which name the route key and the denial reason only and never a category value or a resolved URL.
